meta.temperature_K_convention: Pair is [min_K, max_K]. Use 999 (or any value ≥ 500) for max to mean no practical upper bound in the matcher.

general.description: Highly advanced extremophile organisms that construct semi-enclosed protective bio-spheres. They regulate internal chemistry, temperature, and atmosphere by building a translucent shell around a central organism. Growth is slow and layered, resulting in very old and complex structures.
environmental_context: Often found in isolated patches across flat terrain
Prefer regions with sulfur dioxide atmospheric dominance
Appear as semi-encapsulated spherical or lattice structures
Growth involves continuous shell melting and reformation cycles

color_variants.rule: Color depends on rare planetary materials (NOT star type in canon behavior)

species.description: Sphere-encased organism suspended in a fluid-filled protective membrane with active chemical regulation.
Deltahedron lattice structure forming an external thermal capture framework around a central organism.
Membrane-stabilized lattice organism adapted for low-light photosynthesis through semi-transparent shielding layers.

special_rules: ALL species require thin atmosphere with Sulphur Dioxide dominance
Shell growth involves continuous melt–reform biological cycling
Minimum sample distance is 150m due to clustered distribution
Species selection depends on BOTH atmosphere and planet type
Structures often appear semi-geological due to mineral integration
Recepta colonies are highly localized and sparse across surfaces
Each species represents a different structural adaptation strategy
